verdict.summary: Public connections can be created and used through OAuth with no review. Review (5-10 business days) applies only if you want a Marketplace listing.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min (plus listing prep if you want a Marketplace listing)
verdict.approval_wait: none for OAuth use; 5-10 business days for Marketplace listing (optional)

gates.name: Public connection, your own workspace
gates.unlocks: Create a public connection and authorize it from your own account/workspace.
limits: Installation scope is fixed at creation and cannot be changed
Selected-workspaces connections are subject to the Free workspace block limit (HTTP 403 after grace period)

gates.name: Unlisted public connection (Any workspace)
gates.unlocks: Other Notion users can install and authorize through your OAuth flow without a Marketplace listing.

Rejection reasons include brand/trademark and quality issues

steps.title: Decide: managed Composio auth or your own app
steps.detail: Use Composio managed OAuth to start. Register your own connection if you need your own branding, capabilities, or a Marketplace listing. Internal connections cannot do OAuth.

steps.title: Get a Notion account and development workspace
steps.detail: You need a workspace to act as the development workspace. Docs say creating a connection requires workspace owner (stated for internal connections).

steps.title: Decide installation scope
steps.detail: Choose Any workspace if you may want a Marketplace listing or broad installs. Selected workspaces only is not Marketplace-eligible. It cannot be changed later; you would need a new connection.
gotchas: Wrong choice means recreating the connection and client credentials.

steps.title: Create the public connection
steps.detail: In the Developer portal go to Build > Public connections and click Create new connection. Fill in connection name, development workspace, redirect URIs, installation scope and capabilities.

steps.title: Set the redirect URI
steps.detail: Paste the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config. It must match exactly and have no fragments, relative paths or wildcards.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

steps.title: Choose minimum capabilities
steps.detail: Notion has no scope strings. Select only needed capabilities (Read/Update/Insert content, Read/Insert comments, user info level). Fewer capabilities make admins more likely to install. Changing later forces users to re-authenticate.

steps.title: Copy client ID and secret into Composio
steps.detail: Open the connection's Configuration tab, copy the OAuth client ID and client secret, and enter them in your Composio Notion auth config.

steps.title: Run a test authorization
steps.detail: Authorize through Composio with your account and pick pages in the page picker; the connection only sees selected pages. Verify the token response includes access and refresh tokens and requests send the Notion-Version header.

steps.title: Invite other users to install
steps.detail: With an Any-workspace connection, other users can authorize without a listing. Each teammate must complete the flow themselves.

steps.title: Prepare the Marketplace listing (optional)
steps.detail: Draft listing name, description, category, tags, images and logo. Check brand/trademark use to avoid rejection.

steps.title: Submit the listing
steps.detail: In Listings > Connections, choose Start a new connection listing, attach the public connection and submit the draft to Notion.

steps.title: Wait for Notion review
steps.detail: Expect an email within 5-10 business days. If changes are requested, fix them and resubmit.

requirements.item: Public connection with Any workspace scope

requirements.detail: Needed only before Marketplace listing, not for OAuth use.
Name, description, category, tags, images, logo and the associated public connection.
Must match the one used in the token request.

scopes.effect: Set on the connection instead of OAuth scopes; no scope-level review found. Changing them forces re-authentication.
Highest user-data level; grants user listing/retrieval endpoints. Whether it triggers extra review is unconfirmed.

blockers.cause: Brand/trademark issues, quality concerns, or not meeting baseline criteria.
blockers.fix: Read the rejection email, fix the issues and resubmit.

blockers.symptom: Need Marketplace listing but connection is Selected workspaces only
blockers.cause: Installation scope cannot be changed after creation.
blockers.fix: Create a new public connection with Any workspace and update the client ID/secret in Composio.

blockers.cause: Free workspace block limit is enforced for OAuth connections restricted to selected workspaces.
blockers.fix: Use Any workspace scope or a paid workspace.

blockers.cause: Per-connection limit of 180 req/min (600 on Business/Enterprise). A third-party source claims 3 req/s for unapproved apps; this is unconfirmed.
blockers.fix: Throttle and check the connection's Health tab.

composio.note: Start on Composio managed OAuth for testing. Register your own public connection when you need your own branding, specific capabilities, or a Marketplace listing, then enter its client ID and secret in Composio. Internal connections cannot do OAuth.

evidence.claim: Public connections are created under Build > Public connections via Create new connection with name, development workspace, redirect URIs, installation scope, capabilities.
evidence.quote: Click **Create new connection** and fill in the required fields, including:

evidence.claim: Notion reviews every listing submission.
evidence.quote: The Notion team reviews every listing submission.

evidence.claim: Expect response in 5-10 business days.
evidence.quote: expect to hear back from our team within 5-10 business days via email.

evidence.claim: Rejection reasons include brand/trademark and quality.
evidence.quote: Connections are rejected for various reasons, from brand/trademark issues to quality concerns

evidence.claim: Public connections work without a listing.
evidence.quote: Public connections work independently of Marketplace listings.

evidence.claim: Access is controlled by capabilities, not scope strings.
evidence.quote: These capabilities when put together enforce which API endpoints a connection or token can call

evidence.claim: Fewer capabilities make admin install more likely.
evidence.quote: The fewer capabilities you request, the more likely a workspace admin will be able to install your connection.

evidence.claim: User info with email is a separate, highest level granting user endpoints.
evidence.quote: User capabilities control what user objects show, and they grant access to List all users

evidence.claim: Capability changes require re-authentication.
evidence.quote: users will need to re-authenticate with a connection if the capabilities are changed

evidence.claim: No scope-level review tier found in docs; only the Marketplace security review.
Redirect URI is set in the portal and must match the token request.
evidence.quote: The redirect URI is the URI your users will be redirected to after authorizing the public connection.

evidence.claim: Client ID and secret are on the Configuration tab.
evidence.quote: visit the **Configuration** tab to retrieve your **OAuth client ID** and **OAuth client secret**.

evidence.claim: Redirect URI cannot contain fragments, relative paths, wildcards or be a public IP (third-party).
evidence.quote: It can’t contain URL fragments, relative paths or wildcards, and can’t be a public IP address.

evidence.claim: Authorize and token endpoints, owner=user.
evidence.quote: Always use `user`.

evidence.claim: Token exchange returns access and refresh tokens.
evidence.quote: Notion responds to the request with an `access_token`, `refresh_token`, and additional information.

evidence.claim: Each user must authorize individually.
evidence.quote: only that user can interact with the connection in their workspace

evidence.claim: Users pick pages; denial redirects with an error.
evidence.quote: If the user denies access, they are redirected to the `redirect_uri` with an `error` query parameter.

evidence.claim: Developer portal URL is live but requires JavaScript; form not confirmed.
evidence.quote: Notion JavaScript must be enabled in order to use Notion.

evidence.claim: Health tab added for connections.
evidence.quote: Internal and public connections now have a **Health** tab in the Developer portal.

evidence.claim: Notion has internal, public, and personal access token models.
evidence.quote: Notion supports three authentication models

evidence.claim: Rate limit 180/min on non-Business plans, 600 on Business/Enterprise.
evidence.quote: | All other plans | 180 requests per minute (an average of 3 per second) |

evidence.claim: Third-party claims unapproved public integrations keep 3 req/s; unconfirmed.
evidence.quote: For public integrations that haven’t been approved for higher limits, it’s the same.

evidence.claim: Free workspace block limit enforced for selected-workspace OAuth connections.
evidence.quote: the REST API enforces the existing Free workspace block limit for internal connections and OAuth connections restricted to selected workspaces

evidence.claim: Rate limit uses fixed 60-second window, 600/180 per minute.
evidence.quote: 600 requests per minute on Business and Enterprise plans, and 180 requests per minute on all other plans.

evidence.claim: Notion-Version header 2026-03-11 is used.
evidence.quote: "Notion-Version": "2026-03-11"

evidence.claim: Composio guide: permissions are Capabilities; public integrations use OAuth.
evidence.quote: Notion permissions are configured as **Capabilities**, not traditional scopes.

evidence.claim: Selected-workspaces connections install only in workspaces chosen at creation.
evidence.quote: Only the workspaces you select at creation time.

evidence.claim: Public connection needed when other users install.
evidence.quote: Use an internal connection for team-owned workspace automations, or a public connection when other Notion users need to install your app.

evidence.claim: Creating a connection requires being a workspace owner.
evidence.quote: You are required to be a workspace owner to create a connection.

evidence.claim: Installation scope is set at creation and cannot change.
evidence.quote: Installation scope is set once, at creation time, and can't be changed afterward.

evidence.claim: Security review is needed for Marketplace listing; public connections can be used without listing.
evidence.quote: Public connections must undergo a Notion security review before being listed on the Marketplace. You can create and use a public connection without listing it.

evidence.claim: Only Any-workspace public connections can be listed.
evidence.quote: Only public connections with an installation scope of **Any workspace** can be listed on the Marketplace.

evidence.claim: Listing is a dashboard step with required details, submitted to Notion.
evidence.quote: Fill in the listing details, including: Listing name and description
